subject: Technical validation milestone — benchmark slate & target close
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@healthgrid.com>, Alan Tse <alan.tse@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-04-28T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Technical validation milestone — benchmark slate & target close

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and a proposed MAP milestone for the Technical Evaluation (so we can gate the POC and agree on close criteria). I captured concrete benchmarks, owners, and the dependencies we discussed. Please review and flag any gaps.

Overview (goal): confirm a model + serving configuration that meets HealthGrid's latency and cost targets while preserving answer quality for our clinical triage prompts. Target close date for this milestone (MAP): 2024-05-30.

Benchmarks / success criteria (proposed):
- Quality: intent-accuracy >= 90% on the provided clinical triage prompt suite (sample attached). Hallucination incidents <= 5% (false clinical assertions).
- Latency: P95 end-to-end generation latency <= 300ms for 512-token inputs (measured from request to last token streamed).
- Cost: normalized inference cost per 1M tokens (production-like batch mix) < $50 (Redwood to provide breakdown).
- Throughput: baseline concurrency 40 rps with <= P95 latency target at 512 tokens.

Model shortlist (initial slate we recommend):
- Mistral-Instruct (7B/triage-tuned variant) — strong quality/cost balance
- Llama-2-70B (int8/quantized variant) — if higher accuracy required and infra available
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (q4) — throughput-friendly; check hallucination profile
- Llama-2-13B (q4_1) — low latency, good for edge cases

Evaluation plan / resources needed from HealthGrid:
1) A redacted snapshot (~1k de-identified prompts + expected labels) uploaded to the Drive link or SFTP by 2024-05-03.
2) SRE point-of-contact to enable temporary test VPC access or make a small test endpoint available for throughput tests (required by 2024-05-06).
3) Acceptance checklist owner from HealthGrid to sign off results (name & contact).

Redwood responsibilities (proposed):
- Camila Reyes: customer coordination, MAP updates, and sign-off logistics.
- Jordan Blake: run the latency/throughput benchmarks, produce perf report and cost breakdown.
- Marissa Cole: lead quality/label-based evaluation and hallucination analysis.

Attachments: MAP-draft-tech-eval.xlsx (milestone table), sample-prompt-suite.tsv (labelled prompts), latency-cost-modeling-notes.pdf (initial cost assumptions).

Dependencies / risks:
- Test dataset delivery and redaction — blocks quality runs.
- SRE access timing — blocks throughput/latency validation.
- Model availability in your preferred region for the larger Llama-2-70B tests.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) HealthGrid confirms dataset availability and SRE contact by EOD 2024-05-01.
2) Redwood schedules perf runs for week of 2024-05-06 (Jordan to own).
3) Quality evaluation complete by 2024-05-20; joint review and sign-off meeting week of 2024-05-27.

If that aligns, we will update the MAP spreadsheet with milestones, exact deliverable checkboxes, and owners. Ping me if you want the latency measurement script earlier.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

---

From: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@healthgrid.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Tse <alan.tse@healthgrid.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, HealthGrid SRE <sre@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2024-04-28T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Technical validation milestone — benchmark slate & target close

Appreciate the clear summary, Camila — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can provide a redacted prompt set but need a short NDA addendum confirming de-identified data handling (legal loop). Can Redwood confirm you will use only the labeled prompt set for evaluation and delete any PII after the run?
- On cost: HealthGrid expects a target closer to ~$30 per 1M tokens in production (we currently benchmark internally at that ballpark). Are you able to show a cost plan that hits ~$30 or explain tradeoffs?
- SRE contact: adding our SRE lead Alan (cc). Alan, we'll need a temporary test endpoint or VPN details — can you share availability for the week of 05/06?

Two small asks: please include a short security checklist (SOC2 scope, data residency for the test runs) with the MAP and note whether the 70B runs require specific region capacity.

On first glance the timeline is tight but possible. We'll confirm dataset availability EOD 05/01 after legal confirms the NDA note.

Thanks,
Megan Ortiz
Director, Product — HealthGrid
megan.ortiz@healthgrid.com

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@healthgrid.com>, Alan Tse <alan.tse@healthgrid.com>
Cc: HealthGrid SRE <sre@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2024-04-29T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Technical validation milestone — benchmark slate & target close

Thanks — quick technical clarifications and an owner-level breakdown from our side so the MAP can be prescriptive.

Benchmarks (operationalization notes):
- Latency measurement: we will run end-to-end tests from your test endpoint where possible (measuring request->first-token and request->final-token). P95 <= 300ms target is for request->final-token at 512 tokens. We will also publish P50/P95/P99 and tail latency heatmaps.
- Cost normalization: Redwood will provide two cost lines: (1) raw inference cost at target batch mix; (2) effective per-1M-token cost including autoscaling amortization across reserved capacity. If HealthGrid needs to see a $30/1M plan we can show an aggressive batching+quantization profile for production — but that will likely push model selection towards 13B/7B variants or heavy quantization on 70B.
- Quality eval: Marissa will run n-fold cross-validation on the labelled prompts and supply the confusion matrix + hallucination report. Acceptance = >=90% intent accuracy and hallucinations <=5% overall.

Owners and dates (explicit for MAP update):
- Dataset upload & legal sign-off (HealthGrid) — owner: Megan Ortiz; due: 2024-05-01.
- SRE test endpoint/VPN (HealthGrid) — owner: Alan Tse; due: 2024-05-06.
- Perf runs (Redwood) — owner: Jordan Blake; window: 2024-05-06 -> 2024-05-10.
- Quality runs (Redwood) — owner: Marissa Cole; window: 2024-05-10 -> 2024-05-20.
- Joint review & decision (HealthGrid + Redwood) — owners: Megan & Camila; meeting week of 2024-05-27; target milestone close: 2024-05-30.

Dependencies we call out as blocking:
- If dataset redaction/legal delays > 5 business days we should push the perf window by one week.
- 70B runs: we need region capacity confirmation 72 hours prior to the perf window — otherwise we will default to 13B/40B slate.

I'll prepare the perf script (endpoint test harness) and share via Drive by EOD today. Attaching the initial test harness README and a sample results CSV in the Drive link.

Deal note: deal_id HG-2024-089 — I'll include perf/cost artifacts in the HubSpot deal record.

-Jordan
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@healthgrid.com>, Alan Tse <alan.tse@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-04-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Technical validation milestone — benchmark slate & target close

Great — thanks both. Summary of agreed next steps (finalized for the MAP spreadsheet):
1) Megan / HealthGrid: confirm dataset & sign NDA addendum (owner: Megan) — due 2024-05-01.
2) Alan / SRE: provide test endpoint or VPN access + likely maintenance window constraints (owner: Alan) — due 2024-05-06.
3) Jordan: deliver perf runs + cost breakdown (2024-05-06 -> 2024-05-10).
4) Marissa: deliver quality evaluation (2024-05-10 -> 2024-05-20).
5) Joint review: week of 2024-05-27 — decision & MAP milestone sign-off by 2024-05-30.

I've updated the MAP-draft-tech-eval.xlsx (tab: Milestones) with owners and the acceptance criteria you asked for. Attaching the small security checklist as requested (latency-cost-modeling-notes.pdf includes SOC2/data residency notes).

If anything changes on HealthGrid's side (dataset timing or SRE availability), please flag immediately so we can reprioritize the perf window. Otherwise we'll move ahead with the plan above and I'll book the joint review calendar invite once Jordan and Marissa have preliminary artifacts.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai
